facts.program: Efficiency Nova Scotia Home Energy Assessment (HEA) rebates
facts.claim: Any NS homeowner, any income or heating type, can get up to $5,000 in rebates on upgrades recommended in a Home Energy Assessment.
facts.eligibility: Home in NS, at least 6 months old, grid-connected; upgrades done between initial and final assessment within 12 months; rebates capped at 100% of cost; initial assessment $199, waived for moderate-income households; home must have no renovations started
facts.notes: Rebate cheque mailed within ~90 days of final assessment. 2026-10-05: ENS HEA page re-read in the browser pane ($5,000 maximum, $199 fee, 12 months to finish, rebates within 90 days of final assessment, re-enrol after 6 months). Per-measure amounts in ns-1 to ns-3 come from the Aug 2026 guide PDF, whose text could not be extracted on 2026-10-05. 2026-10-09: ENS home energy assessment page re-read (up to $5,000, $199 fee waived for moderate income, home at least six months old and renovations not started). Per-ton heat pump amounts still rest on the Aug 2026 rebate guide PDF, which could not be opened in the browser. ENS banner: limited information on the federal National Heat Pump Rebate; it will share details.

facts.claim: Ductless mini-split $300 per ton; centrally ducted $500 per ton of newly added capacity; geothermal $600 per ton.
facts.eligibility: Model must be on ENS qualifying list; installed by certified RACM; replacement heat pumps NOT eligible; ducted/compact-ducted mini-splits not eligible
facts.notes: 1 ton = 12,000 BTU/h rated at 47F. 2026-10-03: ENS HEA page still links the Aug 2026 rebate guide. 2026-10-05: HEA page still links the Aug 2026 guide; PDF amounts not re-read (text not extractable), so verified_on stays 2026-10-03.

facts.claim: ENERGY STAR heat pump water heater rebate $800 (via HEA only if no instant rebate was taken at purchase).
facts.eligibility: ENERGY STAR, UEF >= 2.00 (<56 gal) or >= 2.20 (>=56 gal)
facts.notes: Same $800 is available as an instant in-store rebate at participating retailers. 2026-10-03: ENS HEA page still links the Aug 2026 rebate guide. 2026-10-05: HEA page still links the Aug 2026 guide; PDF amounts not re-read (text not extractable), so verified_on stays 2026-10-03.

facts.program: HEA insulation, windows, air sealing, HRV, wood
facts.claim: Attic to R-50 up to $750; exterior walls up to $1,500; basement walls up to $1,200; crawlspace up to $960; ENERGY STAR windows/doors $30 per rough opening; air sealing $200; HRV/ERV $300; wood stove $500; pellet stove/boiler/furnace $1,000.
facts.eligibility: Pro-rated by % of area insulated; semi/end units 75%, middle units 50% for walls/foundation
facts.notes: HRV rebate is $300, not $100. 2026-10-03: ENS HEA page still links the Aug 2026 rebate guide. 2026-10-05: HEA page still links the Aug 2026 guide; PDF amounts not re-read (text not extractable), so verified_on stays 2026-10-03.

facts.claim: Provincial MIR top-up reduced from max $10,000 to max $5,000; stack with HEA ($5,000) for up to $10,000 total.
facts.eligibility: Homeowner, primary residence, primarily NON-electric heat (electric-heated homes not eligible). After-tax household income limits: 1 person $37,260; 2 $77,050; 3 $98,900; 4 $120,750; 5+ $126,500. Must be pre-approved before upgrades. Free HEA.
facts.dates: Reduced after OHPA closed July 2, 2026; applications not yet approved are assessed at new levels
facts.notes: MIR heat pump top-up: $500/ton ductless, $1,500/ton ducted. Old '$15,000 moderate income' claims are WRONG. 2026-10-05: ENS MIR page re-read: limits unchanged, calculated as line 23600 minus line 43500; applications not yet approved are assessed at the new levels.

facts.program: Oil to Heat Pump Affordability (OHPA) in NS
facts.claim: Closed to new applicants as of July 2, 2026; funding fully allocated. Standby list reviewed only if funding frees up.
facts.amount: was up to $10,000 federal + up to $5,000 provincial
facts.notes: 2026-10-05: ENS page re-read; people already on the standby list are reviewed only if more funding becomes available.

facts.claim: Free (no-charge) upgrades such as insulation, draft-proofing and heat pumps for lower-income homeowners, including a free home energy assessment. Long wait times.
facts.eligibility: After-tax household income: 1 person $30,187; 2-4 people $57,075; 5+ $79,163. Homeowner, primary residence.
facts.dates: Open; ~4-6 weeks to hear back on application
facts.notes: Delivered with federal Canada Greener Homes Affordability Program funding. 2026-10-05: ENS page re-read; income limits unchanged; limits reviewed each spring; online or PDF application (PDF takes several weeks longer).

facts.claim: Instant at checkout at participating retailers: smart thermostats for electric heating $45; ENERGY STAR heat pump water heaters $800; heat pump clothes dryers $150; variable-speed pool pumps $200; clothesline kits $5. Also an outside clothes dryer (freestanding) $5.
facts.eligibility: Participating retailers (thermostat also online at getmysa.com)
facts.notes: The $45 thermostat rebate is an Instant Rebate, only for thermostats for electric heating. 2026-10-05: page re-read in full; no end date shown.

facts.claim: Closed to homeowners. Stopped accepting applications April 17, 2025; approved projects had to be complete by March 31, 2026. Still open to non-profits/charities ($0.60/W up to $15,000).
facts.notes: Any '$0.60/watt for homeowners, ~$6,000 on 10 kW' claim is WRONG. 2026-10-05: re-read; ENS still accepts non-profit and charity applications.

facts.claim: Both closed. Grant: last day to submit documents Dec 31, 2025. Loan: no further applications can be approved.

Halifax Solar City: HRM pays the contractor when work finishes; the owner repays through a Local Improvement Charge (LIC) billed separately from regular property taxes, at a fixed 4.75% over 10 years. The charge stays with the property: on sale, pay it off or transfer the balance to the buyer if both agree. Pay off early at any time without penalty. Open to residential homeowners, non-profits, charities, housing co-operatives and places of worship in HRM. Covers solar PV, solar hot water and solar hot air.
facts.amount: financing (4.75% fixed, 10 years), not a rebate
facts.eligibility: HRM property owners in good tax standing
facts.notes: Also https://www.halifax.ca/home-property/solar-projects/property-owner-guide (sale/transfer, early payoff). halifax.ca returns 'Unable to access this page' to automated browsers; read by the site owner on 2026-10-03 and pasted. 'No credit check' appears only on third-party sites; not used.

facts.claim: Free smart thermostat (valued up to $160) professionally installed, for electrically heated homes only.
facts.eligibility: Electrically heated NS homes on residential rate; existing thermostat analog or non-programmable
facts.notes: Not free for all homes. ENS page (2026-10-03): average 12% savings on heating and cooling costs; may also qualify for other free devices (motion sensors, solar security lights, bath fan humidity sensors, faucet aerators, showerheads, thermostatic shower valves). 2026-10-05: re-read; renters need written landlord permission.

facts.claim: Demand-response pilot paused to new enrollments as of April 9, 2026.
facts.amount: existing participants: $30 thermostat / $20 water heater controller (Dec 2026-Feb 2027)
facts.eligibility: existing participants; NS Power customers on a residential or commercial rate code; not for Time-of-Day Rate customers; earn the incentive by taking part in at least 50% of events
facts.dates: paused to new enrolments 2026-04-09; events Dec 1, 2026 to Feb 28, 2027 for existing participants
facts.notes: The $45 thermostat discount is an Instant Rebate, not Eco Shift. 2026-10-05: re-read.

facts.program: Heating Assistance Rebate Program (HARP), Province of Nova Scotia
facts.claim: 2026-27 rebate $400 per household; apply Oct 1, 2026 to Mar 31, 2027 (paper applications postmarked by Mar 31, 2027). Status check online (online applicants only) with confirmation number + postal code; about 8 weeks, longer if more information is needed. Paid by direct deposit if your tax refund is direct deposited, otherwise by mail.
facts.eligibility: Pay your own residential heat and one of: 2025 net income $30,000 or less living alone; combined 2025 net household income $45,000 or less with kids, dependents or other adults; Income Assistance; GIS or the Allowance. Ineligible: heat included in rent, electricity use under 5,000 kWh/yr, investment, seasonal or business properties.
facts.notes: Status: https://www.novascotia.ca/check-status-your-heating-assistance-rebate-application-heating-assistance-rebate-program . Program page: https://www.novascotia.ca/programs-and-services/heating-assistance-rebate-program-harp . Earlier source: news.novascotia.ca 2025-09-26 release. Seniors Care Grant mentioned as separate help; amount not verified. 2026-10-05: apply page re-read; it says about 8 weeks. Single parents need the Canada Child Benefit to count as one.

facts.program: Cape Breton Regional Municipality housing support programs
facts.claim: CBRM's Housing & Development Support Programs are for building new affordable housing and new commercial development: an Affordable Housing Grant ($20,000 or $18,000 per unit, permits 2024 to 2026, all funding allocated), an Affordable Housing Property Tax Adjustment (developers of four or more units) and a Commercial District Development Support Program. None is a home energy or retrofit rebate.
facts.eligibility: New secondary suites, accessory dwellings, two-unit dwellings, apartments, townhouses with a permit issued 2024 to 2026; 10-year affordability
facts.notes: No CBRM heat pump, solar or retrofit program found on cbrm.ns.ca on 2026-10-05; CBRM is not covered by Halifax Solar City (HRM only).
